interest: Documents Occupation policies demilitarizing war memorials, SCAP cultural heritage preservation, and damage photographs from the 1949 Horyuji fire.
overview: This file documents the administration, surveillance, and preservation of monuments, statues, and cultural properties in occupied Japan between March 1947 and October 1949. It details Eighth Army operational directives and Japanese ministerial notifications prohibiting public funerals, ceremonies, and monuments for militarists and the war dead to enforce the separation of religion and state. The records also cover State Department efforts to obtain SCAP Civil Information and Education (CIE) Section files, weekly reports, and microfilms of master card indexes on cultural sites and art collections. Furthermore, the file features extensive investigations, official reports, and damage photographs regarding the catastrophic January 1949 fire at the ancient Horyuji temple's Golden Hall (Kondo) and its murals, along with reporting on the dedication of a Yokohama memorial honoring missionary Dr. James Curtis Hepburn.
